checklist.step: Open an assessment file when an appointment is proposed
actions: Take the proposed appointment from the Board Governance Lead or the CEO's office with the candidate name, target role (officer or director), entity (AIP or named MGA) and target effective date.
Open a fitness-and-propriety file named <candidate>-<role>-<effective date> in the board portal governance workspace.
Record whether the role appears in the Appendix II Plan of Operations officer/director listing — if yes, flag the file 'RMA-listed'.
Notify the HR Business Partner and Employment Counsel that the assessment clock has started.
checklist.done: a dated assessment file exists with candidate, role, entity, effective date and the RMA-listed flag set.

checklist.step: Issue and collect the candidate disclosure questionnaire
actions: Send the candidate the fitness-and-propriety questionnaire from the HRIS onboarding template: criminal history, civil and regulatory proceedings, prior debarment or suspension by any federal agency, insurance-license actions, bankruptcies, and crop-specific conflicts (farming interests, agency ownership, FSA relationships).
Require signature and date; the questionnaire warns that false statements to a federal program are actionable under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
Chase unreturned questionnaires at day 5; escalate to the Corporate Secretary at day 10.
Attach the signed questionnaire to the assessment file.
checklist.done: a signed, dated questionnaire covering criminal, regulatory, debarment and crop-conflict items is on file.

checklist.step: Run the third-party background check
actions: Order the executive-level background package (criminal, federal civil litigation, credit header, education and employment verification) from the screening vendor with the candidate's signed FCRA authorization.
Verify the vendor searched every county and federal district of residence for the past 10 years.
Download the completed report and attach it to the assessment file.
Route any adverse item to Employment Counsel the same day rather than adjudicating it in HR.
checklist.done: the completed background report is on file and any adverse item is with Employment Counsel.

checklist.step: Screen the candidate against SAM.gov exclusions
actions: Open SAM.gov, select Search ▸ Entity Information ▸ Exclusions, and search the candidate's full legal name and any former names from the questionnaire.
Check the classification (Individual), exclusion type and the excluding agency — a USDA or any-agency debarment bars the appointment under 2 CFR 180.
Print the results page (including nil results) to PDF named <candidate>-SAM-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file it in the assessment file.
Repeat the search for any entity the candidate controls that will transact with the AIP.
checklist.done: a dated SAM.gov exclusions capture exists for the candidate and controlled entities, with any hit escalated.

checklist.step: Screen sanctions and watchlists
actions: Enter the candidate's name, date of birth and known addresses into the sanctions screening system and run against OFAC SDN, USDA OIG exclusion and state insurance regulatory action lists.
Disposition every potential match with the match score, the discriminating data point used, and a true/false-match call.
Export the screening result with dispositions and attach it to the assessment file.
Escalate any true match to the Financial Crime AML Officer and Regulatory Counsel before any further onboarding step.
checklist.done: the sanctions screen is complete with every potential match dispositioned in writing.

checklist.step: Check RMA/FCIC sanction and program-compliance history
actions: Search RMA's published administrative sanction and disqualification determinations (7 CFR part 400 subpart R) for the candidate and for prior employers where the candidate held program roles.
Ask the Head of Compliance whether the candidate appeared in any prior RMA compliance finding, Appendix IV training deficiency or SRA suspension matter known to the company.
Record the sources searched, the dates and the nil/positive result on the assessment file.
Route any positive history to Regulatory Counsel for a materiality read against the SRA eligibility provisions.
checklist.done: the RMA/FCIC history check is documented with sources, dates and a counsel read on any positive result.

checklist.step: Verify professional credentials and any producer licenses
actions: Where the candidate holds or claims insurance producer or adjuster licenses, run a producer lookup in NIPR Gateway by NPN and confirm license classes, states and any regulatory actions.
Verify claimed professional designations (CPCU, actuarial credentials, bar admission) directly with the issuing body.
Reconcile the verified record against the questionnaire and flag any discrepancy as an adverse item.
File the NIPR report and verification notes in the assessment file.
checklist.done: licenses and credentials are verified at source and reconciled to the questionnaire with discrepancies flagged.

checklist.step: Assess crop-program conflicts of interest
actions: Review the questionnaire's disclosed farming operations, agency ownership stakes and family relationships with insured producers against the SRA conflict-of-interest provisions and the company's conflicts policy.
Determine whether any disclosed interest requires recusal conditions, divestiture or FCIC disclosure before the appointment.
Draft the conditions (for example recusal from claims involving the candidate's own insured acreage) into the assessment memo.
Obtain the candidate's written acceptance of any conditions.
checklist.done: conflicts are assessed against the SRA provisions with conditions drafted and accepted in writing.

checklist.step: Write the fitness-and-propriety assessment memo
actions: Summarize on the standard memo template: identity verification, questionnaire results, background report, SAM.gov and sanctions screens, RMA history, credential verification and conflicts assessment.
State a recommendation — fit, fit with conditions, or not fit — with the specific evidence behind each adverse-item disposition.
Cite the SRA and 2 CFR 180/417 provisions relied on for any judgement call.
Send the memo to the General Counsel for adjudication.
checklist.done: a complete memo with an evidenced recommendation is with the General Counsel.

checklist.step: Adjudicate and sign the assessment
actions: Read the memo and its exhibits; question any adverse item resolved without a documented discriminator.
Sign the fit / fit-with-conditions / not-fit determination with date, or return the file for further work naming the gap.
For not-fit determinations, notify the Board Governance Lead and the CEO's office in writing the same day.
Record the determination on the assessment file and lock it against edits.
checklist.done: a signed, dated adjudication exists and the sponsoring parties are notified of the outcome.

checklist.step: Obtain board or committee ratification
actions: Place the appointment with the signed assessment determination on the Governance & Nominating Committee agenda in the board portal.
Present the determination and any conditions; for director elections, confirm the proxy or written-consent materials describe the candidate accurately.
Record the committee/board resolution approving the appointment in the minutes.
Attach the minute extract to the assessment file.
checklist.done: a board or committee resolution approving the appointment is minuted and attached to the file.

checklist.step: Effect the appointment only after the assessment closes
actions: Enter the appointment in the HRIS with an effective date on or after the adjudication and ratification dates — the workflow blocks earlier dates.
Load any recusal or divestiture conditions as tracked obligations with owners and due dates.
Notify the Corporate Secretary that the appointment is effective so corporate records are updated.
Confirm signing authorities and bank mandates reflect the new officer where applicable.
checklist.done: the HRIS effective date post-dates adjudication and ratification, with conditions loaded as tracked obligations.

checklist.step: Update the Appendix II Plan of Operations officer/director listing
actions: Add the appointee to the officer/director schedule maintained for the Appendix II Plan of Operations, with name, title and start date.
Where RMA procedures require interim notice of a change in officers or directors, prepare the notification letter for the Regulatory Affairs Manager to send to the RMA regional compliance office.
Otherwise carry the change into the next annual Plan of Operations submission due to RMA by April 1 of the reinsurance year.
File the updated schedule and any notice in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: the Appendix II schedule reflects the appointment and any required RMA notice is prepared or the April 1 carry-forward is logged.

checklist.step: File the complete assessment record for retention
actions: Move the assessment file (questionnaire, background report, SAM.gov and sanctions captures, RMA history check, memo, adjudication, minutes) into the compliance evidence repository under Governance / REG-056 / <candidate>.
Apply the tenure-plus-7-years retention label.
Verify the record is retrievable by candidate name, role and effective date.
Log the file reference on the appointment record in the HRIS.
checklist.done: the full record is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by name, role and date.

checklist.step: Arm ongoing monitoring and re-assessment triggers
actions: Enrol the appointee in the annual batch SAM.gov and sanctions re-screen for all RMA-listed officers and directors.
Create a GRC control task that re-triggers a full assessment on any material event: indictment, regulatory action, new conflict disclosure or RMA sanction.
Set the annual attestation task requiring the appointee to re-confirm the questionnaire answers each reinsurance year.
Confirm the monitoring tasks show the correct owner and next-run date.
checklist.done: annual re-screen, event-driven re-assessment and annual attestation tasks exist with owners and dates.

testing.step: Build the population of appointments effective in the reinsurance year
actions: Extract from the HRIS every officer appointment, and from the board portal every director election or re-election, with an effective date in the reinsurance year (July 1–June 30).
Include appointments at any MGA named in the Plan of Operations, not only the AIP entity.
Reconcile the extract to the Corporate Secretary's minute book so no board-only action escapes the population.
testing.done: the population covers AIP and listed-MGA appointments and reconciles to the minute book.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the Appendix II listing filed with RMA
actions: Obtain the officer/director schedule from the Plan of Operations most recently submitted to RMA (due April 1).
Match every population row to a schedule row; list appointees missing from the filed schedule and schedule names with no appointment record.
Treat every mismatch as an automatic exception for the Regulatory Reporting Analyst to explain.
testing.done: every appointee reconciles to the RMA-filed schedule or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of director elections and RMA-listed officer appointments.
Add a seeded random selection of remaining officer appointments to reach a minimum of 15 files, or the whole population if smaller.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper so the sample is reproducible.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all director and RMA-listed appointments is documented.

testing.step: Verify each sampled assessment file is complete
actions: Open each sampled file in the compliance evidence repository and tick off: signed questionnaire, background report, dated SAM.gov capture, sanctions screen with dispositions, RMA history check, counsel memo, signed adjudication, minute extract.
Record any missing artifact by name — a missing SAM.gov capture or adjudication is a fail, not a documentation gap.
Note the retention label on each file.
testing.done: every sampled file is itemized complete or its missing artifacts are logged as findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the SAM.gov exclusion screen
actions: For each sampled appointee, run a fresh SAM.gov Search ▸ Entity Information ▸ Exclusions query on the full legal name and former names from the questionnaire.
Compare against the filed capture: confirm the original search used the right names and that no exclusion existed at the assessment date.
Capture the re-screen results page into the workpaper.
Report any current exclusion hit immediately to the General Counsel rather than holding it for the report.
testing.done: each sampled appointee has an independent SAM.gov re-screen matching the filed conclusion.

testing.step: Check assessment timing against the appointment effective date
actions: For each sampled file compare the adjudication date and ratification date to the HRIS/minute effective date.
Flag any appointee seated before the adjudication closed as an automatic exception.
Compute the days-early figure for each exception so severity is quantified.
testing.done: every sampled appointment either post-dates its adjudication or is quantified as an exception.

testing.step: Test adverse-item dispositions and imposed conditions
actions: For every sampled file with an adverse item (background hit, potential sanction match, disclosed conflict), re-read the disposition and confirm the discriminating evidence supports it.
Confirm imposed conditions (recusal, divestiture) were loaded as tracked obligations and are being met.
Treat an undispositioned match or an untracked condition as a fail.
testing.done: all sampled adverse items carry supported dispositions and their conditions are demonstrably tracked.

testing.step: Verify ongoing monitoring is armed
actions: In the GRC platform, confirm each sampled appointee appears in the annual re-screen batch and has an annual attestation task with a completed or future due date.
Confirm the event-driven re-assessment control lists the correct trigger events and owner.
Log any appointee absent from monitoring as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled appointee is enrolled in re-screening and attestation with correct owners.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the appointee, the gap, and the SRA/2 CFR provision touched.
Assign root cause (workflow bypassed, screen skipped, schedule not updated) and an owner with a remediation date.
For any appointee seated with an unresolved exclusion or sanction, open a disclosure assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering notice to RMA.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and — where required — a disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold and state a conclusion: effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective.
Have the independent reviewer — who performed none of the sampled assessments — sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Governance & Nominating Committee and the Head of Compliance at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Governance / REG-056 tests.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Build the annual governance policy inventory
actions: Export from the document management repository every policy tagged 'SRA governance set': claims/loss adjustment, underwriting authority, agent/adjuster training, information security, conflict of interest, QC review and record retention.
Record for each the current version, last board-approval date and the SRA/LASH provisions it implements.
Cross-check the list against the policies cited in last year's Appendix II Plan of Operations so nothing filed with RMA is missing from the inventory.
Flag every policy whose approval will be older than 12 months at the next April 1.
checklist.done: a complete inventory exists with version, approval date, SRA mapping and review flags for every policy.

checklist.step: Scan the year's RMA changes that force policy edits
actions: Download from the RMA website the current reinsurance year's SRA and amendments, new LASH handbook releases, Manual 14 updates and Manager's Bulletins issued since the last review.
Map each change to the affected policy — e.g., a LASH revision maps to the claims/loss adjustment policy; an Appendix III change maps to the information-security policy.
Write a change memo listing every required edit with its RMA source and effective date.
Hand the memo to the policy owners with drafting deadlines that hold the T-60 committee pre-read date.
checklist.done: a change memo maps every RMA release of the year to specific policy edits with owners and deadlines.

checklist.step: Update the claims policy to the FCIC claim-form standard
checklist.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Verify the policy requires every indemnity claim to be taken on the Company form meeting FCIC standards and to contain all information section 14 of the Common Crop Insurance Policy Basic Provisions requires before payment.
Confirm the claim-form templates configured in the claims platform match the current FCIC-standard form fields (unit, acreage, share, appraisal, production evidence, adjuster and insured signatures).
Embed the LASH-prescribed adjustment steps and the 3-business-day and weekly transaction-cutoff reporting duties into the policy's procedure references.
Redline the policy and route it to Regulatory Counsel for legal review.
checklist.done: the redlined claims policy enforces the section 14 form standard and matches the configured claim forms.

checklist.step: Refresh the remaining governance policies against the change memo
actions: Collect redlines from each policy owner: underwriting authority (Section IV(d) delegation limits), training (Appendix IV / Manual 14 requirements), information security (Section IV(a)(4)/FISMA), conflicts and QC review.
Check every edit in the change memo appears in a redline; chase owners for any unaddressed item.
Run each redline through Legal Counsel for consistency with the SRA and state law.
Assemble the reviewed set into the committee pack.
checklist.done: every change-memo item is reflected in a legally reviewed redline in the committee pack.

checklist.step: Hold the committee pre-read and resolve comments
actions: Publish the committee pack (redlines, change memo, clean versions) to the Audit/Governance Committee workspace in the board portal at T-60 before the board sitting.
Collect committee comments through the portal's annotation feature and assign each to the responsible policy owner.
Track comment resolution to closure and republish final versions at least 10 business days before the board sitting.
Confirm quorum and agenda placement for the approval resolution.
checklist.done: all committee comments are resolved and final versions are posted ahead of the board sitting.

checklist.step: Obtain board approval of the policy set
actions: Present the policy set with the RMA change memo at the board sitting scheduled before the April 1 Plan of Operations deadline.
Record a resolution naming each approved policy and version number — a blanket 'policies approved' minute is not acceptable evidence.
Capture any board-directed edit, apply it, and note the delegated final approval in the minutes.
File the signed minute extract with the resolution in the board portal.
checklist.done: a board resolution naming every approved policy and version is minuted and filed.

checklist.step: Version, publish and communicate the approved policies
actions: Load each approved version into the document management repository with the new version number, approval date and board-resolution reference, superseding the prior version.
Publish the set to the policy library visible to claims, underwriting and IT staff.
Send the change summary to affected department heads naming what changed and the operative date.
Archive prior versions with their retention labels rather than deleting them.
checklist.done: approved versions are published, prior versions archived and change notices sent to department heads.

checklist.step: Push policy changes into training and attestation
actions: Update the LMS modules that teach the changed policies — in particular the claims-form standard and LASH procedure changes feeding the Appendix IV annual training.
Assign the refreshed modules with attestations to affected staff with a 30-day completion window.
Chase non-completers weekly through their managers.
Export the completion report for the evidence file.
checklist.done: training modules reflect the new versions and the completion report shows the 30-day window enforced.

checklist.step: Cite the approved policies in the Appendix II Plan of Operations
actions: Update the Plan of Operations sections that describe the company's claims, underwriting, training, data-security and QC arrangements to cite the newly approved policy versions.
Cross-check every policy citation in the Plan against the repository version number before submission.
Submit the Plan of Operations to RMA by April 1 through RMA's prescribed submission channel and file the acknowledgement.
Diary the 45-day response window for any RMA comment or information request on the Plan.
checklist.done: the Plan filed by April 1 cites only board-approved versions and the RMA acknowledgement is on file.

checklist.step: Answer RMA comments on governance arrangements within 45 days
actions: Log any FCIC/RMA comment or deficiency notice on the Plan of Operations the day it arrives, with the 45-day response due date computed from the notice date.
Draft the response with the affected policy owner; route commitments through Regulatory Counsel before sending.
Where a comment forces a policy edit, run the edit through the committee/board delegation rather than editing silently.
File the sent response and RMA's acceptance in the evidence repository.
checklist.done: every RMA comment shows a logged date, a counsel-cleared response inside 45 days and any resulting approved edit.

checklist.step: Track mid-year policy amendments through the same approval path
actions: Route any out-of-cycle amendment (new LASH release, incident lessons-learned, RMA finding) through committee pre-read and board or delegated approval before it takes effect.
Record the amendment resolution and update the repository version.
Assess with the Regulatory Affairs Manager whether the amendment changes anything represented in the filed Plan of Operations and notify RMA where it does.
Update the inventory so the annual cycle picks up the new baseline.
checklist.done: no amendment takes effect without an approval resolution, and RMA-material changes are notified.

checklist.step: Monitor policy compliance signals during the year
actions: Load each governance policy into the GRC platform as a control with its owner and 12-month review due date.
Feed QC review findings, claims audit results and RMA compliance findings against the relevant policy control.
Raise a finding when operations diverge from an approved policy rather than amending the policy to fit.
Report control status to the Audit/Governance Committee quarterly.
checklist.done: every policy is a tracked GRC control with findings fed in and quarterly committee reporting.

checklist.step: Escalate lapsed reviews before they breach
actions: Run the inventory monthly and flag any policy within 60 days of its 12-month review anniversary with no scheduled committee slot.
Escalate flagged policies to the Board Governance Lead for an agenda slot or a documented interim extension by the General Counsel.
Log any policy that passes its anniversary unapproved as a compliance exception with a catch-up date.
Report the flag list in the quarterly governance dashboard.
checklist.done: no policy passes its review anniversary without either an approval, a documented extension or a logged exception.

checklist.step: Assemble the annual evidence file
actions: File in the compliance evidence repository under Governance / REG-056: the inventory, RMA change memo, redlines, committee packs, board resolution extracts, publication notices, LMS completion report and the Plan of Operations citation cross-check.
Apply the 7-year retention label to the set.
Verify each artifact is retrievable by policy name and reinsurance year.
checklist.done: a complete, retention-labelled evidence file for the cycle is retrievable by policy and year.

checklist.step: Report cycle completion to the Board
actions: Present a closing memo at the next board sitting: policies approved, RMA comments answered, exceptions logged and open items with dates.
Have the Board note the memo in the minutes as the record that the annual governance review closed.
Hand open items to named owners with dates carried into the next cycle's inventory.
checklist.done: the Board has minuted the cycle-close memo and open items carry named owners and dates.

testing.step: Build the policy population from the inventory and the filed Plan
actions: Extract the governance policy inventory from the document management repository and the list of policies cited in the April 1 Plan of Operations filed with RMA.
Union the two lists — a policy cited to RMA but absent from the inventory is an immediate finding.
Record version numbers and approval dates for every population row.
testing.done: a unioned population of inventoried and RMA-cited policies exists with versions and dates.

testing.step: Reconcile filed citations to approved versions
actions: For each policy cited in the Plan of Operations, compare the cited version against the repository's approved version as at the April 1 submission date.
Flag any Plan citation of a draft, superseded or never-approved version as an exception.
Confirm the Plan's RMA acknowledgement is on file and dated on or before April 1.
testing.done: every Plan citation traces to a board-approved version and the April 1 acknowledgement is verified.

testing.step: Select the sample
actions: Take 100% of the claims/loss-adjustment, information-security and training policies — the SRA-critical set.
Add a seeded random selection of remaining policies to reach at least 8, or the full population if smaller.
Record seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample including all SRA-critical policies is documented.

testing.step: Trace each sampled policy to its board resolution
actions: Open the board portal minutes and locate the resolution naming the sampled policy and version.
Confirm the approval date falls within 12 months of the prior approval and precedes the version's operative date.
Treat a blanket approval that does not name the policy and version as a fail.
Capture the minute extract into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled policy traces to a dated, version-specific resolution captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the RMA change-scan on a sampled basis
actions: Independently list the reinsurance year's SRA amendments, LASH releases and Manual 14 updates from the RMA website.
Compare against the change memo used in the cycle; any RMA change absent from the memo is an exception.
For two sampled changes, verify the corresponding policy text actually changed.
testing.done: the change memo is proven complete against RMA's releases and sampled edits landed in policy text.

testing.step: Verify the claims policy matches the configured claim forms
testing.app: Claims management platform (Guidewire ClaimCenter/Duck Creek Claims)
actions: Open the current claim-form template in the claims platform and compare its fields to the section 14 information requirements the approved policy lists.
Pull three paid indemnity claims from the year and confirm each was taken on the Company form version the policy prescribes.
Flag any paid claim on a superseded or non-standard form as an exception.
testing.done: configured forms and sampled paid claims match the approved policy's section 14 standard.

testing.step: Verify training and attestation followed each approval
actions: For each sampled policy, pull the LMS assignment and completion report for the post-approval training push.
Check assignments went to the affected population within the policy's 30-day window and completions reached the required threshold.
List staff operating under a changed policy with no completed attestation as exceptions.
testing.done: post-approval training and attestation completion is evidenced for every sampled policy.

testing.step: Test the 45-day RMA comment responses
actions: List every RMA comment or deficiency notice on the Plan of Operations logged during the year.
Recompute response due dates as notice date plus 45 days and compare to the actual sent dates.
Confirm each response shows Regulatory Counsel clearance before sending.
Flag late or uncleared responses as exceptions.
testing.done: every RMA comment shows a recomputed on-time, counsel-cleared response or a logged exception.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the policy, the gap and the SRA provision affected.
Assign root cause (missed RMA release, lapsed review, blanket resolution, training gap) with an owner and remediation date.
Route any misrepresentation risk in the filed Plan of Operations to Regulatory Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the no-lapsed-policy threshold with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who drafted or presented none of the sampled policies, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Audit/Governance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under Governance / REG-056 tests.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Define the Protected Information scope for the program year
actions: Query the CMDB for every application, database and file store tagged as processing FCIC Protected Information or policyholder PII — policy admin, claims, the APH yield database, the RMA weekly-submission gateway and agent/adjuster SSN stores.
Interview the Policy Admin Ops Lead and Claims Director / Manager for data flows the CMDB tags miss, including spreadsheets and vendor transfers.
Record each asset with its data elements (SSN, EIN, APH, claim records), owner and hosting location in the ISP scope register.
Have each system owner countersign their scope entry.
checklist.done: the ISP scope register lists every Protected-Information asset with data elements, owner and countersignature.

checklist.step: Map the ISP to the FISMA/NIST control baseline
actions: Load the NIST SP 800-53 moderate baseline into the GRC platform as the control catalog the SRA's FISMA-consistency clause points to.
Map each ISP section to its control families (AC, AU, IA, IR, RA, SC, SI at minimum) and name the implementing control and owner for each.
Mark unmapped baseline controls as gaps with a risk acceptance or a remediation plan — silence is not an option.
Export the mapping as the ISP appendix.
checklist.done: every ISP section maps to SP 800-53 controls with owners, and every baseline gap carries an accepted risk or a plan.

checklist.step: Rewrite the ISP sections that changed during the year
actions: Fold in the year's changes: new systems from the scope register, the current SRA Appendix III wording (including the one-hour incident-reporting duty), architecture changes and lessons from incidents and audits.
State the ongoing risk-based security process explicitly — assessment cadence, treatment, acceptance authority — as Section IV(a)(4) requires.
State the commitment to make internal and external IT security audits and assessments available to FCIC on request.
Route the draft to Legal Counsel and the IT Security Manager for review.
checklist.done: a reviewed ISP draft reflects the year's changes, the risk-based process and the FCIC audit-availability commitment.

checklist.step: Approve the ISP before the Plan of Operations cites it
actions: Sign the annual ISP approval with date and version number.
Present the ISP summary and material changes to the Board risk committee via the board portal and record the ratification minute.
Deliver the approved version reference to the Regulatory Reporting Analyst so the April 1 Appendix II Plan of Operations describes the current program, not a stale one.
Diary the next annual review 12 months out with a T-90 GRC task.
checklist.done: a signed, ratified ISP version exists, is cited in the April 1 Plan, and the next review is diarized.

checklist.step: Publish the ISP and bind staff to it
actions: Publish the approved ISP to the security policy site in SharePoint, superseding the prior version.
Assign the annual security-awareness module covering Protected Information handling and the one-hour incident-reporting duty to all staff and contractors via the LMS, with a 30-day window.
Send system owners their control-ownership extracts so each knows the controls they answer for.
Archive the prior ISP version with its retention label.
checklist.done: the ISP is published, training assigned with a 30-day window, and owners hold their control extracts.

checklist.step: Run the ongoing risk-based security process
actions: Log every new system, vendor or data flow touching Protected Information into the GRC risk register at intake, scoring likelihood and impact.
Review the register monthly with the IT Security Manager; assign treatments with owners and dates.
Record risk acceptances only with the CISO's signature and an expiry date.
Feed accepted risks and open treatments into the annual ISP review input pack.
checklist.done: the risk register shows monthly reviews, owned treatments and CISO-signed, expiring acceptances.

checklist.step: Keep the control mapping live as systems change
actions: Subscribe to CMDB change records for in-scope systems; on any add, retire or re-platform, update the ISP scope register and control mapping within 10 business days.
Re-map controls when a platform migration changes the implementing mechanism (for example on-premises SIEM to cloud).
Flag any in-scope system running longer than 10 business days without mapped controls as an exception.
Report mapping currency in the monthly security operations review.
checklist.done: scope and mappings track CMDB changes within 10 business days and staleness is reported monthly.

checklist.step: Commission the annual independent security assessment
actions: Engage an external assessor to test the ISP against the SP 800-53 moderate baseline over the Protected-Information scope, on a statement of work Procurement runs through the vendor process.
Require a report format producible to FCIC: scope, methodology, findings with severity, and management responses.
Review draft findings with system owners for factual accuracy without negotiating severities.
File the final report in the compliance evidence repository within 30 days of fieldwork close.
checklist.done: an external assessment report over the full scope is final, management-responded and filed.

checklist.step: Track assessment findings to closure
actions: Raise an ITSM task per finding with severity, owner and a due date scaled to severity (critical 30 days, high 60, moderate 90).
Review overdue findings weekly with owners; escalate items 15 days overdue to the CISO.
Attach closure evidence (config export, screenshot, retest note) to each task before closing it.
Summarize open findings monthly to the Board risk committee.
checklist.done: every finding has an owned, dated task, closure evidence, and overdue items show escalations.

checklist.step: Maintain the FCIC audit-production pack
actions: Keep a standing production folder in the compliance evidence repository: current ISP, approval minutes, control mapping, latest internal audit and external assessment reports, and open-finding status.
Refresh the folder within 15 days of any new report or ISP version.
Run a semi-annual drill: assemble the pack as if FCIC had asked, and log the elapsed time against the 45-day response window.
Fix any artifact that could not be produced within the window.
checklist.done: the production pack is current and a drill proves it can be assembled well inside 45 days.

checklist.step: Answer actual FCIC/RMA security requests within 45 days
actions: Log any FCIC or RMA request for IT security audits, assessments or program documents on the day of receipt, computing the 45-day due date.
Assemble the response from the production pack with the Security GRC Analyst.
Route the response through Regulatory Counsel for clearance, including how open findings are characterized.
Send by the RMA-specified channel and file the transmittal and any RMA follow-up.
checklist.done: each request shows a logged receipt date, counsel-cleared response inside 45 days and a filed transmittal.

checklist.step: Wire the ISP to the Appendix III one-hour incident duty
actions: Verify the ISP's incident section states the Appendix III duty verbatim: report any loss or unauthorized disclosure of Protected Information or PII to FCIC within one hour of discovery, suspected or confirmed alike.
Confirm the incident runbook names the RMA notification contact and channel and pre-stages the notification template.
Cross-reference the ISP to the incident response plan version tested under REG-056-C14.
Fix any drift between the two documents within 10 business days.
checklist.done: the ISP and IR plan state the same one-hour FCIC duty, contact and template with no drift.

checklist.step: Flow ISP obligations into vendor contracts
actions: Confirm the CLM security addendum template imposes the ISP's Protected-Information controls, the one-hour incident-notice flow-down and FCIC audit availability on any vendor handling program data.
Reconcile the vendor list from the ISP scope register against CLM to find contracts missing the addendum.
Queue missing addenda for remediation at renewal or sooner for high-risk vendors, coordinating with REG-056-C16 oversight.
Record the reconciliation result in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: every scoped vendor contract carries the security addendum or sits on a dated remediation queue.

checklist.step: Report program health to governance
actions: Present quarterly to the Board risk committee: scope changes, risk register movement, finding closure rates, drill results and any FCIC interaction.
State explicitly whether the program remains FISMA-consistent per Section IV(a)(4) and flag anything threatening the next April 1 representation.
Minute the committee's challenge and any directed actions.
File the quarterly pack in the board portal.
checklist.done: quarterly minuted reporting exists with an explicit FISMA-consistency statement each quarter.

checklist.step: File the year's ISP evidence for retention
actions: File the approved ISP version, scope register, control mapping, approval and ratification minutes, assessment reports and drill logs under InfoSec / REG-056 / <reinsurance year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by year and by artifact type before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the year's full ISP evidence set is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope systems and ISP artifacts
actions: Extract from the CMDB every asset tagged for FCIC Protected Information or policyholder PII and pull the ISP scope register for the same date.
Collect the current ISP version, its control mapping export and the year's approval records.
Record counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: system and artifact populations are extracted with dates and counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile CMDB scope to ISP scope
actions: Match every CMDB Protected-Information asset to a scope-register row and vice versa.
List CMDB assets absent from the ISP scope as automatic exceptions — an unscoped SSN store is a program failure, not a paperwork gap.
Verify countersignatures exist for each sampled scope entry.
testing.done: CMDB and ISP scope reconcile fully or the misses are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Verify the annual approval chain and timing
actions: Trace the ISP version to the CISO signature and the Board risk committee ratification minute in the board portal.
Confirm the approval date is within 12 months of the prior approval and pre-dates the April 1 Plan of Operations that describes the program.
Confirm the Plan's program description matches the approved ISP version in substance.
testing.done: the approval chain is dated, in-window, and consistent with what was represented to RMA.

testing.step: Sample control statements and test they operate
actions: Draw a seeded sample of 15 control mappings across the AC, AU, IA, IR, RA, SC and SI families from the GRC export.
For each, obtain operating evidence from the implementing system — an access-review record, a SIEM alert rule export, an encryption configuration — dated within the period.
Score each control operating / not operating; a mapped control with no operating evidence is an exception.
File the evidence captures in the workpaper.
testing.done: 15 sampled controls are scored with dated operating evidence or logged exceptions.

testing.step: Verify baseline gaps carry acceptances or plans
actions: List every SP 800-53 moderate-baseline control marked unimplemented in the mapping.
Confirm each carries either a CISO-signed, unexpired risk acceptance or a remediation plan with owner and date.
Flag silent gaps — neither accepted nor planned — as exceptions.
testing.done: every baseline gap is either formally accepted or on a dated plan, with silent gaps logged.

testing.step: Test the ongoing risk-based process actually ran
actions: Pull the risk register history and verify monthly review entries exist for at least 10 of the last 12 months.
Trace three new in-scope systems from CMDB intake to a register entry and a treatment or acceptance.
Verify sampled acceptances carry CISO signatures and expiry dates.
testing.done: the register evidences a monthly-run process with intake coverage and signed, expiring acceptances.

testing.step: Verify the external assessment and finding closure
actions: Confirm the year's external assessment report exists, covers the full Protected-Information scope and is filed in the evidence repository.
Sample five findings and trace each to an ITSM task with severity-scaled due date and attached closure evidence or a live escalation.
Recompute due dates from the severity scale and flag closures without evidence.
testing.done: the assessment is on file and sampled findings show dated tasks with genuine closure evidence.

testing.step: Re-run the FCIC production drill independently
actions: Without notice, request the FCIC production pack from the Security GRC Analyst as if FCIC had asked under Section IV(a)(4).
Time the assembly and check the pack holds the current ISP, approvals, mapping and both audit reports.
Compare the elapsed time to the 45-day window and to the last drill's result.
Record any missing or stale artifact as an exception.
testing.done: an unannounced drill produced a complete, current pack comfortably inside 45 days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the system or control, the gap and the SRA/FISMA provision touched.
Assign root cause (scope drift, mapping stale, evidence missing, approval late) with owner and remediation date.
Route any gap that contradicts the filed Plan of Operations description to Regulatory Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and any needed disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the thresholds, with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer from outside the CISO organization sign the workpaper.
Report results to the Board risk committee and Head of Compliance at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper under InfoSec / REG-056 tests in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Scope the annual assessment from the asset inventory
actions: Pull the ISP scope register and the CMDB Protected-Information asset list as the assessment universe — policy admin, claims, APH data warehouse, RMA submission gateway, agent portal, adjuster mobile estate and supporting infrastructure.
Confirm with each system owner that ownership, hosting and data elements are current before scoring starts.
Freeze the scoped list with a date stamp in the GRC platform as the assessment baseline.
Flag any asset added to the CMDB after the freeze for a mid-cycle mini-assessment.
checklist.done: a date-stamped assessment universe reconciled to CMDB and the ISP scope is frozen in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Assemble the threat picture for the crop program
actions: Pull the year's incident and detection history for in-scope assets from Splunk SIEM, including phishing against agency users and credential attacks on the agent portal.
Fold in external threat intelligence relevant to agriculture and federal-program data (PII theft, ransomware against insurers, tax-season SSN fraud).
Note the concentrations peculiar to the program: bulk SSN/EIN records, weekly RMA transmissions and seasonal claim surges after weather events.
Write the threat profile section of the assessment.
checklist.done: a threat profile grounded in SIEM history and program-specific concentrations is written.

checklist.step: Run authenticated vulnerability scans across the scope
actions: In the scanner console, verify every asset in the frozen universe belongs to an active scan group with authenticated (credentialed) scan profiles.
Launch the full scan set and confirm completion status per group; re-run failures rather than accepting partial coverage.
Export the results with CVSS scores and asset mappings; compute coverage as scanned assets over universe assets and record the percentage.
Open an exception immediately for any asset below the 95% coverage line.
checklist.done: authenticated scans cover at least 95% of the universe with exports and the coverage figure recorded.

checklist.step: Commission penetration testing on the exposed surfaces
actions: Test the internet-facing crop surfaces on a written scope: agent/producer portal authentication, the claims intake API, and the file-transfer path used for weekly RMA submissions.
Include an assumed-breach scenario targeting lateral movement toward the SSN/EIN and APH data stores.
Deliver findings with reproduction steps, CVSS scores and affected assets.
Debrief the IT Security Manager and system owners within 10 business days of test close.
checklist.done: a scoped pen test of the exposed program surfaces is delivered with scored, reproducible findings.

checklist.step: Score risks with the SP 800-30 method
actions: For each threat/vulnerability pair on an in-scope asset, score likelihood and impact on the documented 5-point scales, weighting impact up where SSN/EIN bulk records or the one-hour Appendix III reporting exposure is in play.
Derive the risk rating from the scoring matrix and record the rationale sentence on each entry — unexplained scores are returned.
Have the IT Security Manager challenge the top-20 scores in a documented session.
Lock the scored register as the year's findings baseline.
checklist.done: every finding carries scored likelihood, impact, rationale and a challenged, locked rating.

checklist.step: Write and approve the assessment report
actions: Assemble the report: methodology, universe and coverage, threat profile, findings by severity, comparison to last year and the remediation plan summary.
State explicitly that the assessment implements the ongoing risk-based process under SRA Section IV(a)(4) and is available to FCIC on request.
Sign the report and present it to the Board risk committee before the April 1 Plan of Operations submission.
File the signed report in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed report with the Section IV(a)(4) statement is filed and presented to the committee before April 1.

checklist.step: Open a POA&M entry for every finding
actions: Create a Plan of Action & Milestones entry per finding: description, affected assets, severity, owner, milestones and the SLA-derived completion date (critical 30 / high 60 / moderate 90 days).
Link each POA&M entry to its source (scan ID, pen-test finding number, assessment register row).
Reject entries without a named individual owner — team names do not count.
Baseline the POA&M and snapshot it monthly for trend reporting.
checklist.done: every finding has a source-linked POA&M entry with an individual owner and an SLA-computed date.

checklist.step: Cut remediation tickets and drive them to closure
actions: Raise an ITSM ticket per POA&M entry with the fix specification (patch level, configuration change, compensating control) and the SLA date.
Set SLA timers to alert the owner at 75% of the window and page the IT Security Manager on breach.
Require closure evidence on the ticket — patch report, config export or rescan result — before the state moves to resolved.
Reconcile ticket states to POA&M states weekly so neither system drifts.
checklist.done: every POA&M entry maps to a ticket with SLA timers, closure evidence and weekly reconciliation.

checklist.step: Verify fixes by rescan before closing findings
actions: Trigger a targeted rescan of the affected asset once a remediation ticket reports fixed.
Confirm the vulnerability no longer detects at the same plugin/QID; a still-detecting finding reopens the ticket at the same SLA clock, not a new one.
Attach the clean rescan extract to the ticket and the POA&M entry.
Close the POA&M entry only on rescan evidence, with critical/high closures countersigned by the CISO.
checklist.done: findings close only on clean rescan evidence, with CISO countersignature on critical and high items.

checklist.step: Process risk acceptances for what will not be fixed
actions: Require a written acceptance request for any finding the owner proposes not to remediate: business reason, compensating controls and residual risk.
Sign or reject each acceptance; signed acceptances carry an expiry no longer than 12 months and auto-reopen at expiry.
Refuse acceptances on findings that would undermine the Appendix III one-hour reporting capability or bulk SSN protections without committee visibility.
Log acceptances in the GRC register linked to the POA&M entry.
checklist.done: every unremediated finding carries a signed, expiring acceptance or stays open — nothing disappears.

checklist.step: Run continuous scanning between annual assessments
actions: Keep weekly authenticated scans running on internet-facing assets and monthly on internal Protected-Information assets.
Feed new critical/high detections straight into the POA&M and ITSM flow with the same SLAs, without waiting for the annual cycle.
Review scan-coverage drift monthly against the CMDB and re-onboard missing assets within 10 business days.
Report the vulnerability trend in the monthly security operations review.
checklist.done: continuous scans run on cadence, new findings enter the same SLA flow, and coverage drift is corrected monthly.

checklist.step: Fold mid-year changes into a rolling risk view
actions: Run a mini-assessment for every new system, major change or vendor onboarding touching Protected Information, scored on the same SP 800-30 scales.
Update the risk register within 10 business days of go-live.
Escalate any mini-assessment producing a critical rating to the CISO the same day.
Feed the rolling register into next year's annual kickoff.
checklist.done: every material change is scored within 10 business days and criticals escalate same-day.

checklist.step: Report remediation posture to governance
actions: Present quarterly to the Board risk committee: open findings by severity and age, SLA breach counts, acceptance inventory and scan coverage.
Flag any posture change that would alter the risk-process description in the next Plan of Operations.
Minute directed actions with owners and dates.
File the quarterly pack in the board portal.
checklist.done: quarterly minuted posture reporting with SLA and coverage metrics is on file.

checklist.step: Keep the FCIC production set current
actions: Maintain the assessment report, current POA&M snapshot and acceptance register in the standing FCIC production folder alongside the ISP pack.
Refresh within 15 days of the annual report signing and after each monthly POA&M snapshot.
On any actual FCIC/RMA request, hand the set to the Regulatory Affairs Manager for the counsel-cleared 45-day response.
checklist.done: the production folder always holds the current report, POA&M and acceptances, ready for a 45-day response.

checklist.step: File the cycle's evidence for retention
actions: File the signed report, scan exports, pen-test report, POA&M snapshots, closure evidence and acceptance register under InfoSec / REG-056 / <reinsurance year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by year, severity and asset before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: the full assessment-and-remediation evidence set is filed, labelled and retrievable.

testing.step: Build the population of findings, scans and tickets
actions: Export the year's findings register/POA&M from the GRC platform, the scan job history from the vulnerability scanner and the remediation tickets from the ITSM platform.
Pull the frozen assessment universe and the CMDB Protected-Information list as at the freeze date.
Record counts and export dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: findings, scans, tickets and the assessment universe are extracted with dates and counts.

testing.step: Reconcile scan coverage to the asset universe
actions: Match every universe asset to at least one completed authenticated scan in the period and recompute the coverage percentage independently.
List never-scanned Protected-Information assets as automatic exceptions.
Compare the recomputed coverage to the reported figure and investigate any gap over 2 points.
testing.done: coverage is independently recomputed, never-scanned assets are listed, and reporting accuracy is checked.

testing.step: Verify the annual assessment ran and was approved on time
actions: Confirm a signed assessment report exists dated within 12 months of the prior one and before the April 1 Plan of Operations submission.
Check the report contains methodology, universe, coverage, threat profile and severity-ranked findings.
Trace the Board risk committee presentation to its minutes.
testing.done: a complete, signed, committee-presented report inside the 12-month and April 1 windows is verified.

testing.step: Draw the finding sample
actions: Take 100% of critical findings, a seeded random 10 of highs and 5 of moderates from the POA&M export.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Pull the linked source evidence (scan ID or pen-test finding) for each sampled item.
testing.done: a reproducible severity-weighted sample with source links is documented.

testing.step: Re-score sampled findings against the methodology
actions: Independently re-score likelihood and impact for each sampled finding using the documented 5-point scales and the SSN/Appendix III weighting rules.
Compare to the recorded rating; a difference that changes the severity band is an exception, including under-scored criticals.
Record the re-score rationale beside each item in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled finding is independently re-scored with band-changing differences logged.

testing.step: Recompute remediation SLA maths on the sample
actions: For each sampled finding, recompute the SLA date as detection date plus the severity window (30/60/90 days) and compare to the ticket's set date and actual closure date.
Flag closures past SLA without a CISO-signed acceptance, and reopened findings whose clocks were reset.
Quantify days-late for every breach so severity is measurable.
testing.done: SLA dates are independently recomputed with breaches and clock-resets quantified.

testing.step: Verify closure evidence by re-checking the scanner
actions: For 10 sampled closed findings, open the scanner and confirm the vulnerability no longer detects on the affected asset at the closing scan date.
Confirm the clean rescan extract on the ticket matches the scanner's own history.
Treat a closure whose rescan cannot be found in the scanner as a fail, not a filing error.
testing.done: sampled closures are corroborated inside the scanner itself, not just on tickets.

testing.step: Test the acceptance register
actions: List all risk acceptances active in the period and verify each carries a CISO signature, rationale, compensating controls and an unexpired date.
Confirm expired acceptances reopened as findings rather than lingering.
Flag any acceptance covering the Appendix III reporting capability or bulk SSN stores that lacks committee visibility.
testing.done: all acceptances are signed, expiring and correctly reopened, with sensitive ones committee-visible.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the asset or finding, the gap and the SRA provision touched.
Assign root cause (coverage gap, under-scoring, SLA breach, evidence-free closure) with owner and remediation date.
Route anything contradicting the risk-process description filed with RMA to Regulatory Counsel for a disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and any needed disclosure assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the coverage and SLA thresholds with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer from outside the CISO organization sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board risk committee and Head of Compliance at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper under InfoSec / REG-056 tests in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Enforce MFA policy on every Protected-Information application
actions: In the Okta Admin Console open Security ▸ Authentication Policies and confirm each in-scope application (policy admin, claims, APH warehouse, RMA gateway, agent portal) is assigned a policy requiring a phishing-resistant second factor for every sign-on.
Check the app assignments tab so no in-scope application rides on the default password-only policy.
Extend the same enforcement to agency and adjuster external users through the external-identity policy, not just employees.
Export the policy configuration to PDF and file it as the quarter's MFA baseline evidence.
checklist.done: every in-scope app enforces an MFA policy for internal and external users and the config export is filed.

checklist.step: Hunt and close MFA coverage gaps weekly
actions: Run the weekly Okta report of active accounts on in-scope apps with no enrolled second factor or with a policy bypass group membership.
Force enrollment on gap accounts by moving them to the enforce-at-next-login group and notifying the user's manager.
Verify service accounts on the list use certificate or token authentication rather than an MFA bypass.
Log accounts still unenrolled after 14 days as exceptions to the IT Security Manager.
checklist.done: the weekly gap report runs, gap accounts are forced to enroll, and 14-day stragglers are logged.

checklist.step: Control MFA exceptions with expiry
actions: Accept MFA exception requests only through the ITSM catalog item, with business justification and compensating controls stated.
Approve for a maximum of 30 days; the ITSM workflow auto-expires the Okta bypass group membership at the deadline.
Review the open exception list weekly and challenge repeat requesters.
Report exception counts in the monthly security operations review.
checklist.done: all live exceptions are ticketed, 30-day-capped, auto-expiring and reported monthly.

checklist.step: Enforce the encryption standard on data at rest
actions: Verify every database and file store on the ISP scope register holding SSN/EIN, APH yields or claim records shows AES-256 (or platform-equivalent) encryption enabled — TDE for databases, volume or bucket encryption for file stores.
Capture the configuration evidence per store: TDE status query output, storage-encryption console screenshot or IaC policy export.
Confirm database backups and exports inherit encryption rather than landing clear.
File the capture set as the quarter's at-rest evidence and ticket any unencrypted store as a critical finding.
checklist.done: every scoped store shows captured at-rest encryption evidence and gaps are ticketed critical.

checklist.step: Enforce encryption in transit, especially toward RMA
actions: Verify TLS 1.2+ on the agent portal, claims intake API and internal service links carrying Protected Information, using a scan of presented protocols and ciphers against the approved list.

Verify the weekly policy-data transmission to RMA's data acceptance channel uses the RMA-prescribed secure transfer mechanism with current certificates — an expired certificate on that path blocks the transaction-cutoff submission.
Disable any fallback to deprecated protocols found by the scan.
File the scan output and certificate inventory as in-transit evidence.
checklist.done: protocol scans show TLS 1.2+ everywhere in scope and the RMA transfer path has current certificates.

checklist.step: Manage encryption keys on a rotation calendar
actions: Inventory every key and certificate protecting Protected Information with its custodian, algorithm and expiry in the key register.
Rotate keys on the standard's calendar (annually for data keys, per-expiry for certificates) and log each rotation with date and operator.
Alert at 30 days before certificate expiry so the RMA transmission path never lapses mid-season.
Store key material only in the approved vault, never in code or job schedules.
checklist.done: the key register is current, rotations are logged on calendar, and expiry alerts lead certificates by 30 days.

checklist.step: Gate privileged access through the PAM vault
actions: Onboard every privileged account for in-scope infrastructure (database admins, OS admins, RMA gateway operators) into CyberArk safes with check-out, session recording and automatic password rotation.
Block direct privileged login paths that bypass the vault at the network policy layer.
Review safe memberships monthly against the staffing list from the People Analytics / HR Operations Manager.
Export the safe inventory quarterly as control evidence.
checklist.done: privileged access runs only through recorded, rotating vault accounts and memberships are reviewed monthly.

checklist.step: Run the quarterly access recertification campaign
actions: Launch the SailPoint certification campaign within 5 business days of quarter end covering every account and entitlement on in-scope systems, including agency and adjuster external accounts.
Assign line managers as reviewers for user access and system owners for privileged and service accounts.
Chase at day 15 and escalate uncompleted reviews to department heads at day 25 so the campaign closes inside 30 days.
Configure the campaign so a non-response defaults to revoke, not retain.
checklist.done: the campaign covers all in-scope accounts, closes within 30 days of quarter end, and non-responses revoked.

checklist.step: Action revocations from the campaign within SLA
actions: Push every revoke decision to automated deprovisioning where connectors exist, and cut ITSM tickets for manual systems the same day.
Verify each revocation executed by re-querying the target system within 5 business days of the decision.
Record completion evidence on the campaign so every revoke shows an executed date.
Report residual access older than 5 days to the IT Security Manager as exceptions.
checklist.done: every revoke decision shows verified execution within 5 business days or a logged exception.

checklist.step: Enforce joiner/mover/leaver deprovisioning clocks
actions: Consume the HRIS termination and transfer feed into SailPoint so leaver events trigger automatic disablement across in-scope systems within 1 business day.
Strip movers' prior-role entitlements within 5 business days of the transfer effective date rather than letting access accrete.
Include agency terminations reported by the Agency Relations Manager in the same flow for external accounts.
Sample five leavers monthly and verify their accounts are disabled everywhere.
checklist.done: leavers disable within 1 business day, movers shed old entitlements within 5, and monthly samples confirm it.

checklist.step: Monitor control health in the SIEM
actions: Run detections for control failure signals: successful logins to in-scope apps without an MFA event, privileged sessions outside CyberArk, and transfers to RMA over non-approved channels.
Triage alerts within the SOC's severity SLAs and open incidents for confirmed control bypasses.
Feed confirmed bypasses to the IT Security Manager for root-cause fix, not just account cleanup.
Tune detections quarterly against new log sources.
checklist.done: bypass detections run continuously, alerts are triaged in SLA, and confirmed bypasses drive root-cause fixes.

checklist.step: Keep endpoint protection on adjuster and agency devices
actions: Verify CrowdStrike sensor coverage on every corporate laptop used by field adjusters handling claim files and PII in the field.
Check the console's reduced-functionality and stale-sensor lists weekly and remediate within 5 business days.
Enforce disk encryption attestation on those devices through the endpoint policy.
Report field-device coverage in the monthly security operations review.
checklist.done: field and office endpoints show current sensors and disk-encryption attestation with weekly gap remediation.

checklist.step: Reconcile control scope when systems change
actions: On every CMDB add or retire of a Protected-Information system, extend or retire the MFA policy assignment, encryption evidence schedule, PAM onboarding and recertification scope within 10 business days.
Run a quarterly reconciliation of the four control scopes against the CMDB and log misses as exceptions.
Confirm new RMA-facing integrations join the certificate inventory before first transmission.
checklist.done: all four control scopes track CMDB changes within 10 business days and quarterly reconciliations are clean.

checklist.step: Assemble the quarterly control-evidence pack
actions: File each quarter: MFA policy export and gap-report trend, encryption capture set, key-rotation log extract, campaign completion report with revocation verification, and PAM safe inventory.
Label the pack Q<n>-<reinsurance year> with the 7-year retention tag.
Keep the latest pack referenced from the standing FCIC production folder for the 45-day response path.
checklist.done: a labelled, retention-tagged quarterly evidence pack exists and feeds the FCIC production folder.

checklist.step: Report control operation to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the Chief Info Security Officer: MFA coverage percentage, encryption exceptions, campaign timeliness, revocation SLA performance and leaver-clock breaches.
Escalate any metric breaching threshold with a remediation owner and date.
Feed the metrics into the CISO's Board risk committee pack so Section IV(a)(4) attestations rest on data.
checklist.done: quarterly metrics reach the CISO with breaches owned and dated, feeding board reporting.

testing.step: Build the account and configuration population
actions: Extract all active accounts (internal and external) assigned to in-scope applications from Okta, the entitlement inventory from SailPoint, the safe inventory from CyberArk and the store/path list from the ISP scope register.
Pull the four quarterly campaign exports and the year's MFA exception tickets.
Record counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: account, entitlement, safe and configuration populations are extracted with dates and counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the populations to the CMDB scope
actions: Match every CMDB Protected-Information system to an Okta MFA policy assignment, an encryption evidence entry, a recertification scope row and (where privileged) a CyberArk safe.
List systems missing from any of the four control scopes as automatic exceptions.
Verify systems added mid-year joined the scopes within 10 business days of their CMDB record.
testing.done: every scoped system appears in all four control scopes or the miss is logged with its age.

testing.step: Draw the samples
actions: Draw a seeded random sample of 25 user accounts and 10 privileged accounts across in-scope systems, plus 100% of accounts holding an MFA exception during the year.
Select 8 data stores and 5 transmission paths (always including the RMA transfer path) for encryption re-verification.
Record seeds, population sizes and selection dates for reproducibility.
testing.done: reproducible account, store and path samples are documented, RMA path included.

testing.step: Re-verify MFA enforcement on sampled accounts
actions: For each sampled account, open the Okta System Log and confirm recent sign-ons to in-scope apps show a satisfied second-factor event.
Check the account's policy assignment and group memberships for bypass groups.
For exception accounts, verify the ITSM ticket, the 30-day cap and the actual expiry of the bypass.
Flag any sign-on without MFA and without an unexpired exception as a fail.
testing.done: every sampled account shows MFA-satisfied sign-ons or a valid, unexpired exception; anything else is failed.

testing.step: Re-verify encryption on sampled stores and paths
actions: For each sampled store, re-run the TDE/storage-encryption status check with the system administrator watching, rather than accepting the filed screenshot.
For each sampled path, re-scan the presented TLS protocol and cipher and compare to the approved list.
For the RMA transfer path, verify current certificates and the prescribed secure mechanism are in use.
Capture command output into the workpaper.
testing.done: encryption is re-verified live on every sampled store and path, RMA path certificates confirmed current.

testing.step: Test the quarterly campaigns end to end
actions: For each of the four campaigns, verify launch within 5 business days of quarter end, closure within 30 days, and coverage matching the in-scope account population.
Sample 10 revoke decisions per campaign and confirm execution evidence and target-system verification within 5 business days.
Check non-responses defaulted to revoke by inspecting the campaign configuration.
Flag late campaigns, unexecuted revokes and retain-by-default settings as exceptions.
testing.done: all four campaigns show on-time execution, verified revocations and revoke-by-default configuration.

testing.step: Test leaver and mover deprovisioning clocks
actions: Pull 15 terminations (including agency terminations) and 10 transfers from the HRIS/agency feeds across the year.
For each leaver, compare the HRIS termination date to the disable timestamps on every in-scope system and compute the elapsed business days against the 1-day SLA.
For each mover, verify prior-role entitlements were removed within 5 business days.
Quantify every breach in days.
testing.done: sampled leavers and movers show recomputed clock compliance or quantified breaches.

testing.step: Test privileged access stayed inside the vault
actions: Query the SIEM for privileged sessions on sampled in-scope infrastructure and match each to a CyberArk check-out and session recording.
Investigate any privileged session with no vault correlation as a bypass.
Verify the monthly safe-membership reviews ran by inspecting their sign-off records.
testing.done: sampled privileged sessions correlate to vault records and membership reviews are evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the account, store, path or campaign, the gap and the Section IV(a)(4)/Appendix III provision touched.
Assign root cause (policy gap, feed failure, reviewer inaction, certificate lapse) with owner and remediation date.
Route any exposure of SSN/EIN data or the RMA path to the Chief Info Security Officer same-day and assess Appendix III reporting with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date, and sensitive exposures got same-day escalation.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the MFA, encryption and campaign thresholds with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer from outside IT Security and IAM sign the workpaper.
Report to the Chief Info Security Officer and the Board risk committee at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper under InfoSec / REG-056 tests in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.
