checklist.step: Keep the IR plan aligned to Appendix III
actions: Re-read the current SRA Appendix III at each annual revision and confirm the plan states the duty verbatim: report any loss or unauthorized disclosure of Protected Information or PII to FCIC within one hour of discovery, suspected or confirmed.
Verify the plan's severity model carries a mandatory 'Protected Information / PII involved?' gate on every incident, so the one-hour clock cannot be missed by classification.
Confirm the plan defines 'discovery' as the moment any staff member or system identifies a potential loss or disclosure — not the moment of confirmation.
Route the revised plan to the Chief Info Security Officer for annual approval.
checklist.done: the approved plan quotes the one-hour duty, gates every incident on the PII question, and defines discovery correctly.

checklist.step: Pre-stage the FCIC notification playbook
actions: Build the SOAR playbook step that fires on the Protected-Information flag: it opens the notification template, displays the 60-minute countdown, and pages the Incident Response Lead and CISO at T-30 and T-10.

Load the RMA-prescribed notification content into the template: reporting entity, discovery date/time, nature of the suspected loss or disclosure, data categories (SSN/EIN/APH/claim records), affected counts if known, and interim containment.
Store the current FCIC/RMA notification contact and channel from Appendix III in the playbook, with a quarterly task to re-verify it against RMA's latest issuance.
Test-fire the playbook in the SOAR staging environment after every change.
checklist.done: a tested playbook pre-stages the template, countdown, pages and a quarterly-verified FCIC contact.

checklist.step: Train the SOC to start the clock at discovery
actions: Brief every SOC shift that the one-hour clock starts at discovery of a suspected incident — waiting for confirmation is itself a breach.
Add the PII gate to the SIEM triage form so no incident can be saved without answering whether Protected Information may be involved.
Run a monthly five-minute drill card on shift handover covering the declaration steps.
Record training completion in the LMS for every SOC analyst.
checklist.done: every SOC analyst is trained on discovery-starts-the-clock and the triage form enforces the PII gate.

checklist.step: Extend discovery channels beyond the SOC
actions: Publish the internal reporting path (hotline and mailbox routed to the SOC) so claims staff, agents and adjusters can report lost laptops, misdirected mail or exposed records — each such report is a discovery event.
Include the one-hour duty in the annual security-awareness module for all staff and in the agency onboarding pack.
Require vendors handling program data to report suspected incidents to the SOC within 30 minutes by contract, so the company can meet its own 60-minute duty (coordinated with REG-056-C16).
Test the hotline path quarterly with a synthetic report.
checklist.done: non-SOC discovery paths exist, are trained and contracted, and the hotline passes a quarterly synthetic test.

checklist.step: Execute the one-hour notification on live incidents
actions: On any incident flagged for Protected Information, declare discovery in the ITSM ticket with a timestamp and start the SOAR countdown immediately.
Complete the notification template with facts known at the time — Appendix III does not permit waiting to distinguish suspected from confirmed.
Send to the FCIC/RMA contact through the prescribed channel inside 60 minutes and capture the transmission receipt.
Record the sent time in the ticket; compute and store the discovery-to-notification minutes as a ticket field.
checklist.done: each qualifying incident shows a timestamped discovery, a sent notification inside 60 minutes and a stored receipt.

checklist.step: Run containment and forensics without stalling the notice
actions: Isolate affected endpoints via network containment in the endpoint console while the notification proceeds in parallel — containment never delays the one-hour notice.
Preserve volatile evidence and disk images per the evidence-handling procedure with chain-of-custody records.
Determine the scope of records exposed (SSN/EIN counts, APH files, claim documents) and feed updates to the Incident Response Lead for follow-up reports to RMA.
Log all forensic actions in the incident ticket.
checklist.done: containment and forensics run in parallel to the notice, with chain-of-custody and scoped record counts logged.

checklist.step: Send follow-up and closure reports to RMA
actions: Provide RMA the follow-up detail the initial one-hour notice lacked — confirmed scope, affected individuals, remediation — on the cadence RMA directs for the incident.
Route every follow-up through Regulatory Counsel before sending.
Coordinate any policyholder notification obligations under state breach laws with the Privacy Officer so state and federal tracks stay consistent.
File all correspondence in the incident ticket and the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: follow-ups are counsel-cleared, state and federal tracks are coordinated, and all correspondence is filed.

checklist.step: Plan the annual IR exercise
actions: Design this year's scenario around program-specific stakes — for example exfiltration of the APH/SSN warehouse or a ransomware hit during the weekly RMA transmission window — and set exercise objectives including a timed one-hour notification simulation.
Schedule the exercise so it completes before the April 1 Plan of Operations submission, with the date diarized in the GRC platform at T-90.
Invite the CISO, SOC Lead, Regulatory Counsel, Privacy Officer, Claims Director / Manager and a vendor representative where a vendor is in the scenario.
Prepare injects, the scoring sheet and an independent timekeeper.
checklist.done: a dated, objective-scored exercise with a timed notification simulation is scheduled before April 1.

checklist.step: Execute the exercise and time the simulated notification
actions: Run the scenario end to end: detection inject, triage with the PII gate, discovery declaration, playbook firing, template completion and a simulated send to a test address standing in for the FCIC contact.
Have the timekeeper record every timestamp from inject to simulated send and compute the elapsed minutes.
Exercise at least one non-SOC discovery path (hotline report) in the same session.
Capture playbook friction — template gaps, stale contacts, paging failures — verbatim in the observer notes.
checklist.done: the exercise ran end to end with recorded timestamps, an elapsed-minutes result and verbatim friction notes.

checklist.step: Write the exercise report and grade the result
actions: Write the report: scenario, participants, timeline, elapsed notification time against the 60-minute bar, objective scores and findings.
Grade the notification objective pass/fail strictly — a simulated send at 61 minutes fails.
Present the report to the Chief Info Security Officer within 15 business days of the exercise.
File the report in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a graded report with the timed result is presented within 15 business days and filed.

checklist.step: Track after-action items to closure
actions: Raise an ITSM task per exercise finding and per live-incident lesson with owner and a due date no later than 90 days out.
Fold plan and playbook changes back into the IR plan revision and re-test changed playbook steps in SOAR staging.
Review open items monthly with the CISO; items past 90 days escalate to the Board risk committee pack.
Attach closure evidence to each task.
checklist.done: every finding has an owned task closing within 90 days with evidence, and overdue items are escalated.

checklist.step: Verify the RMA contact and channel quarterly
actions: Each quarter, re-check the FCIC/RMA incident-reporting contact and channel in the playbook against the current SRA Appendix III and any RMA bulletin.
Send a no-incident test transmission where RMA provides a test path, or verify channel availability otherwise.
Update the playbook and re-test on any change.
Log the quarterly verification in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: quarterly logged verifications show the notification path is current and reachable.

checklist.step: Report IR readiness to governance
actions: Report to the Board risk committee after each exercise and quarterly thereafter: notification timing performance on live incidents, exercise grade, open after-action items and playbook currency.
State explicitly whether the company can meet the Appendix III one-hour duty today.
Minute directed actions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: minuted governance reporting includes an explicit current-capability statement on the one-hour duty.

checklist.step: File the year's IR evidence for retention
actions: File the approved plan version, exercise report, after-action closures, incident tickets with timing fields, and sent FCIC notifications under InfoSec / REG-056 / <reinsurance year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by incident number and by year.
checklist.done: the year's IR evidence set is filed, labelled and retrievable by incident and year.

checklist.step: Log and disposition any timing breach honestly
actions: Log every notification sent past 60 minutes, and every incident where the PII gate was answered wrongly, as a compliance exception the day it is found.
Open a Regulatory Counsel assessment on whether and how to disclose the late notice to RMA — concealment converts a timing miss into a program-integrity issue.
Record root cause and the corrective change to the playbook or training.
Track the exception to closure with CISO sign-off.
checklist.done: every breach is logged same-day with a counsel disclosure assessment, root cause and signed closure.

testing.step: Build the incident population for the year
actions: Extract every security incident ticket opened in the reinsurance year with its severity, the PII-gate answer, discovery timestamp and any notification fields.
Pull the SOAR playbook execution log and the list of FCIC notifications sent with receipts.
Record counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: the full incident population with gate answers, timestamps and sent notices is extracted.

testing.step: Reconcile detections to tickets so nothing bypassed intake
actions: Sample 20 high-severity SIEM alerts and hotline reports from the year and trace each to an incident ticket with a completed PII gate.
List any alert or report that produced no ticket, or a ticket with the gate unanswered, as an automatic exception.
Check the quarterly hotline synthetic tests actually ran.
testing.done: sampled detections and reports all trace to gated tickets, and hotline tests are evidenced.

testing.step: Re-adjudicate the PII gate on a sample of incidents
actions: Draw a seeded sample of 15 incidents marked 'no Protected Information' and re-read each ticket's facts against the Appendix III definitions.
Flag any incident that plausibly involved Protected Information or PII but never started the clock — these are the dangerous misses.
Refer disputed calls to Regulatory Counsel for a determination and a late-notification assessment where needed.
testing.done: the no-PII population is re-adjudicated and any wrongly-gated incident is referred with an assessment.

testing.step: Recompute the one-hour clock on every notification
actions: For 100% of qualifying incidents, recompute elapsed minutes from the discovery timestamp to the notification transmission receipt.
Verify the discovery timestamp against the earliest evidence of awareness (alert time, hotline call log) — a back-dated discovery is a fail, not a fix.
List every notice over 60 minutes with its elapsed time.
Verify each sent notice contains the required content: entity, discovery time, nature, data categories, counts if known.
testing.done: every qualifying incident shows recomputed elapsed minutes from an evidence-corroborated discovery time.

testing.step: Verify the annual exercise happened and was graded
actions: Confirm an exercise report exists for the reinsurance year, dated before April 1, with participants, timeline and the timed notification result.
Check the timekeeper's timestamps support the reported elapsed minutes.
Confirm the scenario exercised the PII gate and at least one non-SOC discovery path.
Treat a year with no completed exercise as an automatic fail.
testing.done: a graded, timestamp-supported exercise before April 1 is verified or the miss is failed.

testing.step: Trace after-action items to closure
actions: Trace every exercise finding and sampled live-incident lesson to an ITSM task with owner and due date.
Verify closure evidence on completed tasks and escalation records on any past 90 days.
Confirm playbook changes from findings were re-tested in SOAR staging.
testing.done: all findings trace to owned tasks with evidence, escalations, and re-tested playbook changes.

testing.step: Re-verify the notification path is current
actions: Open the SOAR playbook and compare the stored FCIC/RMA contact and channel to the current SRA Appendix III text.
Check the quarterly verification log shows four completed checks for the year.
Fire the playbook in staging and confirm the countdown, template and paging steps still execute.
testing.done: the playbook contact matches Appendix III, quarterly checks are logged, and a staging fire succeeds.

testing.step: Test breach handling of any late or missed notice
actions: For every recomputed breach, verify a same-day exception log entry, a documented disclosure assessment and the decision rationale.
Confirm the corrective change (playbook, training, gate wording) actually shipped.
Verify no breach was closed without CISO sign-off.
testing.done: every breach shows honest logging, a counsel assessment, a shipped fix and signed closure.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per test exception naming the incident or artifact, the gap and the Appendix III provision touched.
Assign root cause (gate error, clock started late, stale contact, exercise slip) with owner and remediation date.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner and date.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the zero-late-notification threshold with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who played no role in the sampled incidents or exercises, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Board risk committee and Head of Compliance at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper under InfoSec / REG-056 tests in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Refresh the curriculum to the year's RMA requirements
actions: Download the current reinsurance year's Manual 14 and SRA Appendix IV from the RMA website and extract the training topic and hour minimums for agents and loss adjusters, new and experienced tracks separately.
Map each requirement to an LMS module — new-hire curriculum, annual refresher, LASH procedure updates and any RMA-mandated special topic for the year.
Fold current-year LASH handbook changes into the adjuster modules so training matches the standards claims are adjusted under.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the curriculum map before assignments open.
checklist.done: an approved curriculum map ties every Manual 14/Appendix IV requirement to a current LMS module.

checklist.step: Build the training roster from every channel
actions: Pull the agent roster from the agency/producer management system via the Agency Relations Manager and the adjuster roster (staff and contract) from the Claims Director / Manager.
Load every individual into the LMS with their track: new agent, experienced agent, new adjuster, experienced adjuster.
Classify experience using the SRA definitions of Experienced Agent and Experienced Loss Adjuster — years and volume thresholds — not manager judgement.
Reconcile the roster count to active appointments and open claim assignments so no transacting individual is missing.
checklist.done: the LMS roster covers every transacting agent and adjuster with an SRA-definition-based track.

checklist.step: Assign training with deadlines ahead of the transacting cutoff
actions: Assign each individual their track's modules with a completion deadline at least 30 days before the earliest date they will sell, service or adjust for the crop year (driven by the state sales closing dates).
Configure the LMS to record hours per topic so completions evidence the Manual 14 hour minimums, not just a checkbox.
Send weekly chase reports of non-completers to agency principals and claims managers.
Block new work assignment for anyone past deadline by flagging them to the Distribution Operations Manager and Claims Director / Manager.
checklist.done: assignments carry hour-tracked deadlines ahead of transacting dates and non-completers are blocked from new work.

checklist.step: Administer the CAPP proficiency examinations
actions: Schedule the required CAPP proficiency examinations for experienced loss adjusters through the LMS exam engine under proctored conditions.
Apply the pass mark and retake rules RMA prescribes; log every attempt with score and date.
Move adjusters who exhaust retakes onto the full training track — they may not adjust as 'experienced' without a pass.
Export the exam ledger for the certification file.
checklist.done: every experienced adjuster shows a logged CAPP attempt history and no failed adjuster works the experienced track.

checklist.step: Verify licenses alongside training
actions: Run each agent through NIPR Gateway by NPN and confirm an active crop line of authority in every state where they sell, plus active appointments with the company.
Verify adjuster licenses in states that license crop adjusters.
Flag any lapsed license or appointment to the Agency Relations Manager for suspension of transacting rights until cured.
Attach the license verification export to the certification file.
checklist.done: every roster member shows verified licenses and appointments or a logged suspension of transacting rights.

checklist.step: Track field training days for new adjusters
actions: Record the supervised field-adjustment days Manual 14 expects for new loss adjusters, with the supervising experienced adjuster named on each entry.
Verify supervisors themselves hold current certification before their supervision counts.
Sign off each new adjuster's field record before they adjust independently.
File the field-training ledger with the LMS records.
checklist.done: every new adjuster shows a signed field-training ledger supervised by certified adjusters.

checklist.step: Chase completion to 100% before the cutoff
actions: Run the completion dashboard weekly in the final 60 days, split by agency and claims office.
Escalate agencies under 90% completion at T-30 to the Head of Distribution; claims offices to the Chief Claims Officer.
Record the terminal status for every individual: completed, extended with justification, or barred from transacting.
Freeze the completion data as the certification snapshot once the cutoff passes.
checklist.done: a frozen snapshot shows every individual completed, formally extended or barred — no silent gaps.

checklist.step: Reconcile the certified roster against actual transacting records
actions: Pull the agents of record on the year's eligible crop insurance contracts from the policy administration platform and the adjusters on the year's claims from the claims platform.
Match every transacting individual to a completed-training row in the certification snapshot.
Investigate every mismatch — an untrained agent of record or adjuster on a paid claim is an exception with policy-level impact.
Document the reconciliation with counts and differences resolved.
checklist.done: every transacting agent and adjuster matches a completed-training row or is logged as an exception.

checklist.step: Draft the annual certification of compliance
actions: Draft the certification on the RMA-prescribed form language: all agents and loss adjusters performing services on eligible crop insurance contracts completed required annual training and hold current certification, including CAPP proficiency where applicable.
Attach the certified roster with training dates, hours and exam results as the supporting schedule.
List any barred individuals and the controls preventing them from transacting.
Route the draft to Regulatory Counsel for wording review.
checklist.done: a counsel-reviewed draft certification with the supporting roster schedule is ready for signature.

checklist.step: Obtain the certifying officer's signature
actions: Walk the certifying officer through the reconciliation results, exception list and the evidence trail before signature — the officer signs a federal-program representation.
Obtain the signature and date on the certification.
Log the signed certification in the compliance evidence repository.
Brief the officer on the correction duty if post-filing facts contradict the certification.
checklist.done: the certification is signed on an evidenced walkthrough and logged, with the correction duty briefed.

checklist.step: File the certification with RMA by the deadline
actions: Submit the signed certification with the Appendix II/IV package to RMA through the prescribed submission channel by April 1 of the reinsurance year.
Capture the submission receipt or acknowledgement and attach it to the certification record.
Diary the 45-day window for any RMA follow-up question.
Confirm the filed version matches the signed version byte-for-byte.
checklist.done: the certification is filed by April 1 with a captured receipt and the follow-up window diarized.

checklist.step: Answer RMA follow-ups within 45 days
actions: Log any RMA question on the certification the day it arrives with the computed 45-day due date.
Assemble per-individual transcripts and exam records from the LMS to answer roster-level questions.
Route the response through Regulatory Counsel, especially where an individual's status was borderline.
File the response and RMA's closure in the certification record.
checklist.done: every RMA follow-up shows a logged date and a counsel-cleared response inside 45 days.

checklist.step: Handle mid-year joiners without breaking the certification
actions: Enrol every mid-year agent or adjuster hire into the track curriculum immediately at onboarding, with completion required before they transact.
Gate their system access to policy and claims platforms on LMS completion status via the joiner workflow.
Append completed mid-year joiners to the certification roster maintained for next year's filing.
Sample five mid-year joiners quarterly to confirm the gate held.
checklist.done: mid-year joiners train before transacting, the gate is sampled quarterly, and the roster stays current.

checklist.step: Correct the certification if facts break it
actions: On discovering any individual who transacted uncertified after filing, assess with Regulatory Counsel whether a corrected certification or disclosure to RMA is required.
Quantify the affected policies and claims with the Compliance Analyst for the disclosure decision.
File any correction through the same RMA channel with the certifying officer's countersignature.
Log the event as an exception with root cause and remediation.
checklist.done: post-filing discoveries drive a counsel-assessed, officer-countersigned correction decision that is logged.

checklist.step: File the cycle's evidence for retention
actions: File the curriculum map, LMS completion export, CAPP exam ledger, license verifications, reconciliation workpaper, signed certification and RMA receipt under Training / REG-056 / <reinsurance year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by individual name and by year.
checklist.done: the full certification evidence set is filed, labelled and retrievable by individual and year.

testing.step: Build the transacting population independently
actions: Extract the agents of record on all eligible crop insurance contracts and the adjusters on all claims for the crop year directly from the policy and claims platforms — not from the training roster.
De-duplicate to a unique-individual list with the states and volumes each transacted.
Record counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independent transacting-individual population exists from source systems, not the roster.

testing.step: Reconcile the transacting population to the certified roster
actions: Match every transacting individual to a row on the roster attached to the filed certification.
List individuals who transacted but do not appear on the roster as automatic exceptions — these undermine the certification itself.
List roster members with no transactions as scope notes, not exceptions.
testing.done: every transacting individual matches the certified roster or is an automatic exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample
actions: Take a seeded random 25 agents and 15 adjusters from the matched population, plus 100% of experienced adjusters who adjusted claims over the year's large-loss threshold.
Include at least three mid-year joiners and three individuals from the barred/extended list.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date for reproducibility.
testing.done: a reproducible, risk-weighted sample including joiners and barred individuals is documented.

testing.step: Re-verify training completion in the LMS
actions: Open each sampled individual's LMS transcript and verify module completions, recorded hours against the Manual 14 minimums, and completion dates before their first transaction of the crop year.
Check the modules completed match the curriculum map for their track and year — completing last year's modules does not count.
Flag completions dated after the individual's first policy sale or claim assignment as fails with the day-gap quantified.
testing.done: sampled transcripts show current-year, hour-sufficient completions pre-dating first transactions.

testing.step: Re-verify CAPP examinations for experienced adjusters
actions: Trace each sampled experienced adjuster to a passing CAPP score in the exam ledger with attempt dates and proctoring evidence.
Verify failed-and-retaken sequences followed the retake rules and that nobody adjusted between a failure and a later pass on the experienced track.
Confirm adjusters who exhausted retakes were moved to the full training track before further assignments.
testing.done: every sampled experienced adjuster shows a valid pass and no adjusting occurred in a failed window.

testing.step: Re-verify licenses and appointments at source
actions: Run five sampled agents through NIPR Gateway and confirm the crop line of authority and company appointment were active in each state and on each date they sold.
Compare against the license verification export in the certification file for accuracy.
Flag any sale during a lapsed-license window as an exception with policy identifiers.
testing.done: sampled agents show source-verified active licenses and appointments on their transaction dates.

testing.step: Test the transacting gates actually held
actions: For sampled barred or past-deadline individuals, query the policy and claims platforms for any transaction during their barred window.
For sampled mid-year joiners, verify system access was provisioned only after LMS completion by comparing access grant dates to completion dates.
Treat any transaction inside a barred window as a certification-breaking fail.
testing.done: barred windows show zero transactions and joiner access post-dates training completion.

testing.step: Verify the filed certification and its timing
actions: Confirm the signed certification matches the frozen snapshot, carries the certifying officer's signature and was submitted by April 1 with a captured receipt.
Verify the exception list disclosed in the certification matches the reconciliation workpaper.
Check any RMA follow-up was answered inside 45 days with counsel clearance.
testing.done: the filed certification is signature-complete, snapshot-consistent, on time, and follow-ups were timely.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the individual, the gap and the Manual 14/Appendix IV requirement touched.
Assign root cause (roster miss, gate bypass, stale curriculum, exam shortcut) with owner and remediation date.
Route any untrained individual who touched paid claims to Regulatory Counsel for a certification-correction and RMA-disclosure assessment.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date and any needed correction assessment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the zero-untrained-transactor threshold with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer, who assembled no part of the roster, sign the workpaper.
Report to the Head of Compliance, Chief Claims Officer and the audit committee at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper under Training / REG-056 tests in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.

checklist.step: Maintain the register of program third parties
actions: Extract from the procurement platform every active supplier and cross-mark those performing program services or touching Protected Information: MGAs, independent adjusting firms, IT/cloud processors, print-mail houses and data providers.
Ask the Claims Director / Manager and Policy Admin Ops Lead quarterly for engaged firms that bypassed procurement, and add them.
Record for each: services, data accessed (SSN/EIN, APH, claim files), contract reference and risk tier.
Reconcile the register to the third-party arrangements described in the current Plan of Operations.
checklist.done: a complete tiered register reconciles to procurement, operational knowledge and the filed Plan of Operations.

checklist.step: Tier vendors by data exposure and program criticality
actions: Score each registered vendor on the documented matrix: volume of Protected Information handled, role in the claims/underwriting chain, and substitutability.
Assign tier 1 to any vendor holding bulk SSN/EIN or APH data or adjusting claims; tier 2 to limited-data processors; tier 3 to no-data suppliers.
Record the tier and rationale in the GRC platform — tier drives the assessment depth and reassessment clock.
Re-tier on any service change reported through the procurement platform.
checklist.done: every vendor carries a scored, recorded tier that drives its assessment cadence.

checklist.step: Run pre-contract security due diligence
actions: For tier-1 vendors, obtain and review the current SOC 2 Type II report — read the exceptions and complementary user entity controls, not just the opinion — or run the full security questionnaire with evidence where no report exists.
For tier-2, run the standard questionnaire covering encryption, access control, incident response and subcontractor use.
Check the vendor entity in SAM.gov Exclusions — a debarred vendor cannot serve a federal program.
Write the risk decision (approve / approve with conditions / reject) into the GRC record; the procurement platform gate holds POs until this closes.
checklist.done: each new vendor shows a tier-appropriate, evidence-based risk decision and a clean SAM.gov check before contract.

checklist.step: Bind Appendix III obligations into the contract
actions: Attach the crop-program security addendum in the CLM to every in-scope contract: FISMA-consistent controls over Protected Information, encryption standards, the duty to report suspected incidents to the company SOC within 30 minutes (so the company can meet its one-hour FCIC duty), FCIC/RMA audit rights, subcontract flow-down and data destruction at exit.
For adjusting firms and MGAs, add the Section III(a)(3) clause requiring SSNs for every agent and adjuster before they perform services.
Log the executed addendum version against the vendor record in the CLM.
Queue legacy contracts missing the addendum for amendment at renewal, or immediately for tier-1 vendors.
checklist.done: every in-scope contract carries the executed addendum with the 30-minute flow-down and SSN clause logged in CLM.

checklist.step: Collect SSNs before any agent or adjuster performs services
actions: Collect the SSN of every agent and loss adjuster — employed or vendor-supplied — at appointment or engagement, on the W-9/collection form, into the agency/producer management system.
Configure the system to block activation of a producer or adjuster code until the SSN field validates, so nobody can be assigned policies or claims without it.
Obtain from each adjusting firm a certified roster of its adjusters with SSNs before the firm receives claim assignments.
Encrypt SSN storage and restrict access per the C13 control standard.
checklist.done: no producer or adjuster code activates without a validated SSN, and vendor rosters arrive certified before assignments.

checklist.step: Transmit SSNs to FCIC with the weekly data submission
actions: Include the agent and loss adjuster SSNs on the records submitted to FCIC through RMA's data acceptance process in accordance with FCIC procedures, by the weekly transaction cutoff date covering their first service activity.
Reconcile RMA's acceptance/rejection response file each week and correct rejected SSN records before the next cutoff.
Track any contract flagged by RMA for a missing SSN — no reinsurance is paid on it until the SSN is provided — and escalate to the CFO's Capital Management Manager for the reinsurance impact.
File the weekly acceptance confirmations in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: SSNs ride the weekly submissions by cutoff, rejections are cured next cycle, and flagged contracts are escalated.

checklist.step: Verify vendor personnel controls at onboarding
actions: Require each tier-1 vendor to evidence background screening and annual security training for personnel touching Protected Information.
Confirm vendor adjusters appear on the company's LMS certification roster (REG-056-C15) before claim assignments, since the training duty follows the person.
Obtain the vendor's named security contact and incident-reporting path and load both into the SOC's playbook contacts.
Record the verification in the GRC vendor record.
checklist.done: tier-1 vendor personnel show screening, training and a loaded incident contact before work starts.

checklist.step: Grant vendors least-privilege, monitored access
actions: Provision vendor users through sponsored external identities in the IAM platform with MFA enforced and access scoped to the specific application roles their contract requires.
Set automatic expiry on vendor accounts at the contract end date from the CLM.
Include vendor accounts in the quarterly SailPoint recertification with the Vendor Manager as reviewer.
Alert the SOC on vendor-account anomalies (off-hours bulk queries against SSN/APH stores).
checklist.done: vendor access is sponsored, MFA-enforced, contract-expiring, recertified quarterly and SOC-monitored.

checklist.step: Run annual reassessments by tier
actions: Reassess tier-1 vendors annually on their anniversary: refreshed SOC 2 report review, incident history, subcontractor changes and a repeat SAM.gov check; tier-2 biennially by questionnaire.
Raise findings with owners and severity-scaled due dates in the GRC platform.
Suspend new work orders through the procurement platform for vendors with overdue critical findings.
Record each reassessment with its evidence and decision.
checklist.done: tier-1 vendors show in-window annual reassessments with tracked findings and enforced consequences.

checklist.step: Exercise the incident flow-down
actions: Include a vendor-origin scenario in the annual IR exercise (REG-056-C14): a vendor reports a suspected disclosure and the company's one-hour FCIC clock runs from the company's discovery.
Verify each tier-1 vendor's 30-minute reporting path annually with a synthetic test message to the SOC.
Debrief failures with the Vendor Manager and require corrective evidence from the vendor within 30 days.
Log exercise and test results in the GRC vendor record.
checklist.done: vendor-origin scenarios are exercised, 30-minute paths are tested annually, and failures carry corrective evidence.

checklist.step: Disclose third-party arrangements in the Plan of Operations
actions: Update the Appendix II Plan of Operations sections describing MGA, adjusting-firm and material-processor arrangements from the vendor register before the April 1 submission.
Verify every disclosed arrangement carries a current contract and closed due diligence in the register — disclosing an unassessed vendor to RMA is its own finding.
Submit with the Plan by April 1 and file the acknowledgement.
Notify RMA of material third-party changes mid-year where RMA procedures require it.
checklist.done: the April 1 Plan discloses register-verified arrangements and mid-year material changes are notified.

checklist.step: Enforce secure offboarding at contract end
actions: On termination or expiry, trigger the offboarding checklist from the CLM: access revocation same day, return or certified destruction of Protected Information within 30 days, and subcontractor attestations.
Obtain the signed destruction certificate and file it against the vendor record.
Confirm the IAM contract-expiry disabled all vendor accounts by re-querying the IAM platform.
Update the register and next Plan of Operations disclosure.
checklist.done: exited vendors show same-day access revocation, a 30-day destruction certificate and updated disclosures.

checklist.step: Track vendor exceptions and remediation
actions: Log every gap — vendor live without due diligence, missing addendum, overdue reassessment, unprovisioned SSN — as an exception with owner and remediation date.
Escalate SSN gaps immediately: quantify affected contracts with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst since reinsurance is withheld until cured.
Sign each remediation closure; the CISO co-signs where Protected Information was exposed.
Report open exceptions monthly to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: every gap is logged, SSN gaps are quantified and escalated, and closures are signed.

checklist.step: Report the vendor security posture to governance
actions: Report quarterly to the Chief Info Security Officer and the Board risk committee pack: register size by tier, reassessment currency, open findings, SSN reconciliation status and incidents of vendor origin.
Flag any posture change affecting the Plan of Operations third-party description.
Minute directed actions with owners and dates.
checklist.done: quarterly posture reporting with SSN status reaches governance and directed actions are minuted.

checklist.step: File the year's vendor-oversight evidence
actions: File the register snapshots, due-diligence packs, executed addenda, reassessment reports, weekly SSN acceptance confirmations and destruction certificates under Vendor / REG-056 / <reinsurance year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label.
Verify retrieval by vendor name and by year.
checklist.done: the year's vendor evidence set is filed, labelled and retrievable by vendor and year.

testing.step: Build the vendor population independently
actions: Extract all suppliers with spend or active contracts in the reinsurance year from the procurement platform and the CLM, and independently mark those whose services touch program data or operations.
Compare against the third-party register — a program vendor absent from the register is an automatic exception.
Record counts and extraction dates in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently built vendor population is reconciled to the register with misses logged.

testing.step: Reconcile the register to the filed Plan of Operations
actions: Compare the register's MGA, adjusting-firm and material-processor entries to the arrangements disclosed in the April 1 Plan of Operations.
List undisclosed active arrangements and disclosed-but-inactive ones as exceptions for the Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
Verify the Plan's submission acknowledgement is dated on or before April 1.
testing.done: register and Plan disclosures reconcile and the April 1 timing is verified.

testing.step: Draw the vendor sample
actions: Take 100% of tier-1 vendors onboarded in the year, a seeded random 10 of continuing tier-1 vendors and 5 of tier-2.
Include every vendor that exited during the year for offboarding testing.
Record seed, population sizes and selection date for reproducibility.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering new, continuing and exited vendors is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform due diligence traces on sampled vendors
actions: For each sampled vendor, verify the GRC record holds a tier rationale, a due-diligence pack (SOC 2 review notes or questionnaire with evidence) and a dated risk decision pre-dating the contract signature.
Re-run the SAM.gov Exclusions search on the vendor entity and compare to the filed check.
Read the SOC 2 review notes to confirm exceptions and user-entity controls were actually addressed, not just filed.
Flag decisions post-dating contract signature as fails.
testing.done: sampled vendors show pre-contract, evidence-based decisions and clean re-run SAM.gov checks.

testing.step: Verify the contract addendum on each sampled vendor
actions: Open each sampled contract in the CLM and confirm the executed security addendum with the Appendix III controls, 30-minute incident flow-down, FCIC audit rights and — for MGAs/adjusting firms — the SSN clause.
Check legacy contracts queued for amendment actually amended on schedule.
Flag any live in-scope contract without the addendum as an exception with its data exposure noted.
testing.done: every sampled contract carries the executed addendum or is logged with its exposure.

testing.step: Reconcile SSN provisioning end to end
actions: Extract all agents and adjusters (employed and vendor-supplied) who performed services in the year from the policy and claims platforms.

Match each to a validated SSN in the agency/producer management system and to an accepted record in the weekly RMA submission confirmations, checking the acceptance pre-dates or meets the cutoff covering their first service.
List anyone who performed services before their SSN reached FCIC — quantify the affected contracts, since reinsurance is withheld on them.
Verify RMA rejection files were cured by the following cutoff on a sample of five weeks.
testing.done: every service performer traces to an FCIC-accepted SSN by the governing cutoff or is quantified as an exception.

testing.step: Test vendor access and its expiry
actions: For five sampled vendors, list their user accounts in the IAM platform and verify MFA enforcement, role scoping to contracted services and expiry dates matching CLM contract ends.
For exited vendors, confirm all accounts disabled on or before the termination date and the destruction certificate is on file within 30 days.
Verify vendor accounts appeared in the year's quarterly recertification campaigns.
testing.done: sampled vendor access is scoped, expiring and recertified, and exits show timely disablement plus destruction certificates.

testing.step: Verify reassessments and the 30-minute path tests
actions: Check each sampled continuing tier-1 vendor completed its annual reassessment within the anniversary window, with findings tracked to severity-scaled dates.
Verify the annual synthetic test of each tier-1 vendor's 30-minute incident path ran and failures carry corrective evidence.
Confirm work-order suspension actually engaged for any vendor with overdue critical findings.
testing.done: reassessments are in-window, path tests are evidenced, and suspension consequences demonstrably engaged.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception naming the vendor or individual, the gap and the SRA provision touched (III(a)(3), IV(f)(2), Appendix III).
Assign root cause (register miss, gate bypass, cutoff slip, stale addendum) with owner and remediation date.
Route unprovisioned-SSN findings to the CFO's team for the reinsurance impact and to Regulatory Counsel for RMA communication.
Carry open exceptions into next year's test as mandatory retests.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, date, and SSN findings carry financial and regulatory routing.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: State the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — against the due-diligence, addendum and SSN thresholds with evidence references.
Have the independent reviewer from outside vendor management and procurement sign the workpaper.
Report to the Chief Info Security Officer, Head of Compliance and the Board risk committee at the next sitting.
File the signed workpaper under Vendor / REG-056 tests in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion and committee reporting date is on file.
